clue.text: Disagreement with rule in section of library?

indicators.note: in says the letter for rule sits inside the library section's name

parts.note: fiction is a section of a library, shelving novels

explanation.surface: A librarian quarrels over a regulation in one part of the library.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction between people is conflict or discord, a synonym for disagreement.

clue.text: Tropical fruit from the linden tree?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a tropical fruit grows on the linden tree.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the small green citrus fruit; the other is the common British name for the linden tree, a different plant entirely.

clue.text: Plant left with outer protection

indicators.note: with here means the letter for left is held within the protective word

parts.note: a cover is an outer protection

explanation.surface: A plant has been left with a protective covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing plant of the pea family, often three-leaved.

clue.text: React badly when witch enters old city

indicators.note: enters says the word for witch goes into the jumbled letters
badly signals that the letters of react are put together wrongly

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: Someone reacts badly when a witch arrives in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'React badly' reads as someone's response to a witch, but 'badly' is the anagram signal, giving CARTE; 'enters' splits it as CART...E.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient Phoenician city in North Africa destroyed by Rome.

clue.text: Most important maiden possibly on horseback

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, so a maiden is one example of an over
riding means being on horseback

explanation.surface: A young woman may be the most important rider on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a girl; in cricket a maiden is an OVER of six balls with no runs scored, and 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An overriding concern is the paramount one, taking precedence over all others.

clue.text: Make a fuss in case there's drug

indicators.note: in places the drug's letter inside the word for case

parts.note: a crate is a wooden packing case
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a fuss in case drugs are present.
explanation.walkthrough: To create, in British informal speech, is to complain loudly or make a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: In British colloquial usage, to create means to kick up a row or complain noisily.

clue.text: Take extraordinary care and list items

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters of care and list are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An instruction to take great care and list some items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' looks like part of the phrase 'take extraordinary care' but it rearranges CARE and LIST together.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles are things or objects, especially individual goods, much like items.

clue.text: Sentimental sue finishing off man

indicators.note: finishing off means the final letter of sue is removed

parts.note: Gary is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone sentimental decides to sue and finish off a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing off' cuts the E from the end of SUE, leaving SU.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugary describes something cloyingly sweet in feeling, as sentimental writing is.

clue.text: Commercial presentation makes a daughter green

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A TV commercial makes a young woman jealous with envy.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is green in heraldry, a common crossword usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a commercial promotion of a product, a short presentation selling it.

clue.text: Pain of champion hard to admit

indicators.note: to admit means to let something in, so the letter for hard goes inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert or champion
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A champion finds it painful to admit defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: A rev. Eating out — one with special dietary requirements

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order and reset

explanation.surface: A reverend eating out is someone with special dietary needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating out' reads as dining at a restaurant, but 'out' is the anagram signal for A, REV and EATING together.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian avoids meat, so needs particular food when catered for.

clue.text: Better trained as someone to repair the machine?

explanation.surface: A better-trained person is wanted to repair the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is more physically fit after training; the other is a mechanic who assembles or mends machinery.

clue.text: Period at home with friend at the end

parts.note: a term is a period of time
in means at home
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone spends a period at home with a friend at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminally means finally, in a way that comes last or is fatal.

clue.text: Sees a learner is being taken in by reverse of wise person

indicators.note: being taken in by says the earlier pieces go inside the wise person's word
reverse of says the word for wise person is read backwards

parts.note: a seer is a prophet or wise person
L is the standard abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates
taken as written

explanation.surface: A learner is fooled by the opposite of a sage and finally sees the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' gives REES; 'being taken in by' means the A, learner and IS go inside that reversed wise person. 'Sees' here means understands, not looks at.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp or understand it, just as seeing a point means understanding it.

clue.text: Fellow appearing in Bolton or Manchester

indicators.note: appearing in signals letters found running through the place names

explanation.surface: A man turns up in Bolton or Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'BoltoN OR MANchester'; Bolton and Manchester are towns in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman is a man's name, and fellow is a common crossword stand-in for any man.

clue.text: A nude seen around end of the road in Welsh town

indicators.note: seen around says the outer pieces surround the inner ones

parts.note: bare means naked or nude

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A naked person is spotted near the end of the road in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of the road' looks like one idea but splits into the end of 'the' (E) plus the road; 'seen around' wraps the nude pieces around ERD, splitting after AB.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a town in the Cynon Valley of south Wales.

clue.text: Composer I conducted around America

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for conducted is read backwards

parts.note: led means conducted or guided

explanation.surface: A musician says they conducted an orchestra on a tour of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it means turned round, giving DEL; Frederick Delius was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Delius was an English composer of orchestral works.

clue.text: Man is turning up outside part of hospital as a guard

indicators.note: outside says the turned letters go around the hospital department
turning up in a down clue means the man's name and is are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Len is a man's name
taken as written
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A man turns up outside a hospital ward to stand guard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads upwards, giving SINEL from the man and 'is' together; 'outside' wraps that around the hospital department after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or watchman posted to keep guard.

clue.text: Detection using sixth sense at first impressed all lookers-on

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, the so-called sixth sense

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A psychic's detection by sixth sense initially impressed every onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for spying or noticing, the act of discovering something.

clue.text: Refusals to accept this person's candidates for election

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the possessive goes inside the refusals

parts.note: noes are refusals or negative votes
mine means belonging to me, this person speaking

explanation.surface: Voters' refusals stop someone accepting their own election candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is the setter speaking, so 'this person's' is MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominees are people put forward for a post or office.

clue.text: Man to reside beset by gold

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the verb sits inside the word for gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to live is to reside

explanation.surface: A man chooses to live surrounded by gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver is a man's name, and man is a common crossword stand-in for any male name.

clue.text: Plead with somebody: go away!

parts.note: to beg is to plead
one means someone or somebody

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with another person, then tells them to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old-fashioned command meaning leave at once.

clue.text: Report that woman's not sagging in quarrel!

explanation.surface: Someone reports a woman's figure is still firm in the middle of a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading describes a woman's chest staying up; the second is the British informal term for a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase says a woman's bust stays high and firm; as a noun it is a noisy row or fight.

clue.text: Random pair of records — one successful, the other not

definitions.text: pair of records — one successful, the other not

explanation.surface: Two records were released, one a chart success and the other a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means haphazard or unpredictable; literally it describes one chart-topper and one failure.

clue.text: Vessel that's large crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the river's letter goes inside the word for large

parts.note: big means large

explanation.surface: A big ship is crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: Resist male beast

explanation.surface: A male animal resists being handled.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck a trend is to oppose it; a buck is the male of deer, rabbits and similar animals.

clue.text: Where wine is kept, tradesperson said

indicators.note: said signals a word that is heard rather than written

parts.note: a seller is a trader

explanation.surface: A merchant explains where the wine is stored.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground room, traditionally used to store wine.

clue.text: Set up article in the course of meal with editor

indicators.note: in the course of means during, so the article goes within the meal

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article was set up during a meal with the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the course of' sounds like a meal's courses but here means inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a project or company is to start or establish it.
